subject: botany
question_text: Describe the process of fertilization in angiosperms.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book pp.19-20, LAQ 2). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Book scan errors cleaned here: 'Triple fussion', 'sygamy', 'endosp[erm] nucleus' with missing letters. The book defines mesogamy in this answer as entry 'through integument (or) funiculus'; its own LAQ 4 and the standard definition say through the integuments — this card writes integuments. FIGURE SCOPE: the book's 'Longitudinal section of a flower showing growth of pollen tube' is redrawn as a simplified pistil (stigma-style-ovary) with the tube reaching the embryo sac.

page_header: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 8 marks

steps.label: Definition and the tube's path
lines: The fusion of the male and female gametes is
called fertilisation.
After pollination the pollen grain germinates
on the stigma; the pollen tube grows down
through the style and reaches the ovary.
steps.why: The process has a fixed order — pollination, germination, tube growth, entry, fusion — so the answer opens with the definition and the tube's journey to the ovary.
common_mistakes: Starting at the ovule and skipping the stigma-style path.
Treating pollination as fertilisation. Pollination only delivers the grain; fusion is fertilisation.
steps.memory_tip: Order of events: land (stigma) → grow (style) → enter (ovule) → fuse (gametes).
steps.margin_note: Definition plus the stigma-to-ovary journey — two sentences open the answer.

steps.label: Entry into the ovule
lines: The pollen tube enters the ovule in any one
of three ways:
Porogamy — through the micropyle. Eg: Ottelia
Chalazogamy — through the chalaza.
Eg: Casuarina
Mesogamy — through the integuments.
Eg: Cucurbita
steps.why: Whatever the route, the destination is the same embryo sac — the three names only describe which doorway the tube uses: the natural pore, the base, or through the side walls.
common_mistakes: Mixing the examples across routes. Pair them: Ottelia-micropyle, Casuarina-chalaza, Cucurbita-integuments.
Writing porogamy as the only route — the other two exist and carry names.
steps.memory_tip: PORE-ogamy through the pore (micropyle); CHALAZ-ogamy through the chalaza; MESO = middle, through the wall between the two ends.
steps.margin_note: Three lines, one route + one example each — a compact table in words.

steps.label: Diagram — pollen tube reaching the sac
steps.why: One picture holds the whole journey: grain on the stigma, tube down the style, entry into the ovule, tip at a synergid beside the egg — the same structures the written steps name.
common_mistakes: Drawing the tube stopping at the ovary wall — it must reach the embryo sac inside the ovule.
Labelling the egg where a synergid is. The tube's tip meets a synergid first.
Leaving the pollen grain off the stigma — the tube must start from a grain.
steps.memory_tip: Draw pistil first (stigma, style, ovary), ovule inside, then one bold line from grain to synergid.
steps.margin_note: The tube must be drawn from the grain to inside the ovule — a half-drawn tube loses the mark.

steps.label: Entry into the synergid
lines: Whichever way it enters the ovule, the pollen
tube enters a synergid through the filiform
apparatus.
The tip of the tube ruptures and releases the
two male gametes into the synergid.
steps.why: This is the hand-over moment: the filiform apparatus receives the tube, the tip bursts, and the two male gametes are set free for the two fusions that follow.
common_mistakes: Sending the tube straight into the egg. It always passes through a synergid first.
Releasing one male gamete. Two are released — both are needed for double fertilisation.
steps.memory_tip: All three roads meet at the synergid: filiform apparatus in, tip bursts, two gametes out.
steps.margin_note: Two sentences: filiform-apparatus entry, then the release of both male gametes.

steps.label: Double fertilisation
lines: Double fertilisation consists of two events:
1. Syngamy: the first male gamete fuses with
the egg cell to form the diploid zygote (2n).
2. Triple fusion: the second male gamete
fuses with the secondary nucleus of the
central cell to form the primary endosperm
nucleus (3n).
steps.why: Both male gametes fuse, and with different partners — that pair of fusions is what 'double fertilisation' means, and the ploidies (2n zygote, 3n endosperm nucleus) prove which fusion is which.
common_mistakes: Writing 2n for the primary endosperm nucleus. It is 3n: two polar nuclei + one male gamete.
Calling triple fusion 'three gametes fusing'. It is one gamete + the (already fused) two polar nuclei.
Spelling errors under pressure: it is syngamy, and fusion (the book's scan even prints 'fussion').
steps.memory_tip: Gamete 1 + egg = 2n zygote. Gamete 2 + 2 polar nuclei = 3n. One fusion makes the plant, the other makes its food.
steps.margin_note: Name both events with their ploidies — 2n and 3n written explicitly earn the 2 marks.

steps.label: Significance
lines: The zygote develops into the embryo and the
primary endosperm nucleus develops into the
endosperm, the nutritive tissue of the seed.
Double fertilisation is a characteristic
feature of angiosperms.
steps.why: The closing line answers 'so what': each fusion product has a destiny (embryo, endosperm), and the whole double event is unique to angiosperms — the sentence examiners expect at the end.
common_mistakes: Stopping after the two fusions without their fates.
Claiming double fertilisation occurs in gymnosperms too — it is the angiosperm signature.
steps.memory_tip: Two fusions, two futures: baby plant (embryo) and its packed lunch (endosperm).
steps.margin_note: The boxed fates plus 'characteristic of angiosperms' close the answer.

insider_note: The two ploidies are the examiner's checksum — a script that writes 2n beside the zygote and 3n beside the primary endosperm nucleus signals the whole process was understood.
